claims.text: Controlled aging can precipitate a fine Ni2Si secondary phase within an MnNiSi matrix.
The proposed Ni2Si secondary phase is ductile.
Fine Ni2Si precipitation will improve both yield strength and ductility of MnNiSi.
Fine Ni2Si precipitation can retain the large magnetocaloric effect of MnNiSi.
The initial MnNiSi alloy has a strong magnetocaloric transition.
The initial MnNiSi alloy is intrinsically brittle and has low fracture strain.
The brittleness and low fracture strain of the initial alloy arise from its single-phase microstructure.
Aging at approximately 500–600 °C for several hours can induce homogeneous nanoscale Ni2Si precipitation in MnNiSi.
An inert atmosphere is required to prevent oxidation during aging.
Keeping the aging temperature below the solidus will preserve the magnetostructural transition.
The aging treatment will produce uniformly distributed nanoscale Ni2Si precipitates that are coherent or semi-coherent with the MnNiSi matrix.
Fine Ni2Si precipitates will pin grain boundaries.
Fine Ni2Si precipitates will impede crack propagation.
Grain-boundary pinning and impeded crack propagation will enhance ductility and yield strength.
The primary magnetostructural phase will remain essentially unchanged after controlled aging.
Preserving the primary magnetostructural phase will preserve the magnetocaloric effect.
Relative to untreated or as-cast MnNiSi, the aged material will have higher yield strength and fracture strain.
After aging, the magnetic entropy change and transition temperature will remain within approximately 10–15% of the untreated alloy values.
Excessive aging can cause precipitate coarsening and create crack-initiation sites that reduce mechanical toughness.
Overaging may alter the magnetic transition.
